item.title: French students vow to continue protests, saying ministers’ pledges not enough
item.description:
French authorities suspended the use of stun grenades Wednesday after a teenager lost his hand during clashes with police, as demonstrations over school conditions spread to more than 40 cities. Protesters’ weekslong blockade of schools is the most visible aspect of a multifaceted national crisis, as public workers strike, bond yields rise to multidecade highs , and France’s traditional parties reckon with the far-right. But one proximate trigger of public discontent may have been overlooked: a ban on phones in schools enforced last month. Following the loss of this “comfort object” — which provides entertainment and connection — the “high school student has opened their eyes to a situation that has suddenly become unbearable ,” a French teacher argued in Grand Continent. — Brendan Ruberry

item.title: Flávio Bolsonaro’s Advance in Brazil’s Election Is Grim News for the Climate
item.description:
This story was originally published b y the Guardian and is reproduced here as part of the Climate Desk collaboration. More fire, more ash, more crime, more death. And a globally important ecosystem driven ever more rapidly towards a point of no return. That is the prospect for the Amazon rainforest for at least the next four years if Flávio Bolsonaro holds on to the lead he established this week in the first round of Brazil’s presidential election. This appears to be of far more concern to the outside world than to voters in Latin America’s biggest, richest, and most biodiverse nation. The far-right son of the former president and jailed coup-monger Jair Bolsonaro won 47 percent of the vote , putting him in pole position before the October 25 runoff with the incumbent, Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva, who was backed by 44.2 percent. item.title: Maricarmen, the 87-year-old woman whose eviction shook Spain, dies
item.description:
NASA Margaret Hamilton, the trailblazing computer scientist whose software was crucial in putting the first astronauts on the moon, has died at age 90. Hamilton led the software engineering team at the Massachusetts Institute of Technology (MIT) for NASA’s Apollo program. She is credited with popularizing the term “software engineering” through her work and with saving the Apollo 11 mission. In 1969, just minutes before the spacecraft was due to land on the moon, Apollo 11’s onboard computer started flashing alarms indicating an error. Mission Control was debating whether to abort the entire landing. However, the software that Hamilton and her team built came to the rescue, telling the onboard computer to prioritize essential tasks—the landing itself—and canceling less important ones as part of its recovery mechanism. “If the computer hadn’t recognized this problem and taken recovery…

item.title: Canada suspends plans to expand assisted dying to people with mental illness
item.description:
Legislation is an effort by ruling Liberals to address growing clash over who has access to doctor-assisted death Canada ’s federal government said on Wednesday it would advance legislation to prevent people whose sole health condition is mental illness from accessing euthanasia, an effort by the ruling Liberal party to address a clash in the country over who has access to physician-assisted death. Under the current rules, people whose sole underlying medical condition is a mental illness have been barred from accessing medical assistance in dying (Maid) to end their lives. But that ban – due to be lifted in March – has divided lawmakers over whether to permit this expansion of the Maid program. item.title: What the Paramount and Warner Bros deal means for you
item.description:
Paramount Skydance on Tuesday closed its deal to acquire Warner Bros. Discovery, ending a dramatic, yearlong process that rattled Hollywood, Wall Street and Washington. Why it matters: The deal creates one of the largest entertainment behemoths in the world and makes David Ellison — a lesser-known figure outside of Hollywood — one of the most powerful people in culture and business. Zoom in: The combined entity, rebranded Skydance, will house three major movie studios (Paramount Pictures, Warner Bros. Pictures and Skydance), two global streamers (Paramount+ and HBO Max) and two major news networks (CNN and CBS). It will also create a cable juggernaut, marrying Paramount's Viacom channels, such as MTV, VH1 and Comedy Central, with WBD's cable networks, including TBS, TNT, Food Network and Discovery.
